text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like NVDA on 2026-09-18, the median realised return over the next 5 sessions was 0.86%, with a mean of 0.65% and a standard deviation of 3.8%. The distribution is slightly right-skewed (skew 0.214), but the left tail contains drawdowns as deep as -7.34%, meaning the path risk matters more than the central tendency for sizing purposes.

[state]
The engine selected these analogs because the current state combines several distinctive features. NVDA sits -6.03% from its 52-week high (z-score 0.564) after a 60-session return of 11.82% (z-score 0.39). Its own 20-session realised volatility is elevated at 45.77% (z-score 0.824), while the benchmark 20-session volatility is unusually compressed at 9.16% (z-score -0.574). WTI crude oil has surged 19.24% over 20 days (z-score 1.124), the most extreme macro feature in the vector. Mean absolute overnight/weekend gaps are 1.28% (z-score 0.718), dollar volume is below average with a z-score of -0.62, and there are 45 calendar days to the next earnings release (z-score 0.663) with 0 scheduled events in the next 5 sessions (z-score -0.496). This mix of high idiosyncratic volatility, low market volatility, an oil shock, and proximity to a 52-week high pulls in Technology names alongside Energy and ETF Sector analogs that shared this specific cross-asset tension.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a median return of 0.86% and a mean of 0.65%. Returns finished above zero in 56% of the episodes and below zero in 44%. The spread is wide: the 10th percentile is -4.04%, the 25th percentile is -2.03%, the 75th percentile is 3.07%, and the 90th percentile is 4.68%. The extremes range from -7.34% to 10.25%. The histogram shows the most populated bin is around -0.38% (10% share), with a secondary cluster near 1.82% (12% share) and 3.29% (10% share). The bad tail is dominated by specific recent episodes. The closest analog overall is NVDA itself on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2999), which went on to lose -5.9% over 5 sessions with a max adverse excursion of -7.44%. Another close match, XLK on 2026-08-13 (distance 0.4178), returned -4.02% with a max adverse excursion of -4.38%. On the upside, NVDA on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.4317) returned 9.66%, and MU on 2024-01-16 (distance 0.4111) returned 3.45%. The conformal prediction interval, scaled at 1.31 and fitted on 2019-2022 data, spans from -4.12% to 5.83% (width 9.95%), achieving 80.8% out-of-sample coverage on 2698 test queries.

[tails]
A position can end the week near flat and still be un-holdable through the middle. Across the 50 analogs, the median maximum adverse excursion was -2.01%. At the 25th percentile, the worst intra-week drawdown reached -3.77%, and at the 10th percentile it hit -4.38%. Conversely, the median maximum favourable excursion was 2.55%, reaching 4.39% at the 75th percentile and 6.71% at the 90th percentile, yielding a reward/risk ratio of 1.27. In terms of breach probabilities, 8% of the analog episodes saw a 5% drawdown at some point during the 5 sessions. No episode in the set breached a 10%, 15%, or 20% drawdown threshold. The 90% Value at Risk on the terminal return is 4.04%, and the 90% Conditional VaR is 5.46%.

[stress]
When conditioned on historical stress regimes, the baseline picture deteriorates materially in several scenarios. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario produces a median forward return of -5.4%, which is -6.26% worse than the baseline, with a 10th percentile of -14.14% and a 58.3% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; however, central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, making it a sample of one regime rather than a forecast. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare yields a median of -3.02% (-3.88% delta vs baseline) and a 10th percentile of -6.18%, though it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019 that flatters late-window analogs. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario shows a median of -2.42% (-3.28% delta) and a 10th percentile of -8.44%, but the nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind gives a median of -2.11% (-2.97% delta) and a 10th percentile of -8.61%; the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2025-04 tariff shock produces a median of -2.7% (-3.56% delta) and a 10th percentile of -8.21%, but policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. The 2023-03 regional bank stress is the only window that improves the baseline, with a median of 1.51% (+0.65% delta), though the very short window means the analog set is dominated by a handful of sessions. Among the shock scenarios, a +2 sigma VIX spike shifts the median to -0.18% (-1.04% delta) with a 10th percentile of -7.47%, but VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. A +1.5 sigma rate path re-pricing gives a median of -0.39% (-1.25% delta); this uses DGS3MO/T10Y2Y levels as proxies, and transmission to a single name depends on duration and balance sheet features not present here. The liquidity air pocket shock yields a median of 0.83% (-0.03% delta), but gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, bounding reference-market gap risk only. Earnings day conditioning gives a median of 1.61% (+0.75% delta), but earnings dates for foreign private issuers come from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than 8-K Item 2.02 dates. FOMC day conditioning results in a median of 0.07% (-0.79% delta), but only 92 decision days exist in the calendar, so the analog set is small and highly overlapping. Crypto contagion yields a median of 0.8% (-0.06% delta), but the BTC feature is a market-wide proxy and any name-level linkage to crypto flows is not identified. China ADR de-rating gives a median of -0.06% (-0.92% delta), but delisting and audit-access risks are structural and will not appear in a price/vol feature space. No scenarios were skipped by the engine.

[limits]
This analysis retrieves historical conditional distributions; it does not forecast future prices or probabilities. The engine's own validation states explicitly: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Specifically, the analog conformal width is 10.4% versus 10.2% for the raw analog at matched coverage, while the unconditional name-in-time band achieves 82.4% coverage with a narrower 10.12% width. The directional hit rate is 50.1%, indistinguishable from a coin flip. The PIT chi-square statistic is 208.6 against a 5% critical value of 16.92, confirming the raw distribution fails uniformity. Only 3 of the 50 retrieved analogs are NVDA itself, drawn from 31 distinct sessions across 33 distinct symbols, meaning the bulk of the distribution comes from other names sharing similar feature vectors. The dataset spans 2513 sessions and 71 symbols from 2016-09-20 to 2026-09-18, heavily weighted toward 2025 (16 analogs) and 2026 (22 analogs). Price data is sourced keyless from api.stockanalysis.com, and earnings dates rely on SEC full-text search clustered at 6 calendar days. Every stress scenario carries its own caveat regarding sample size, survivorship, or structural changes that limit direct application to the current tape.
